_doc: Screw drivers as data for the driver_access check (mm). The tool path is a cylinder of the tool's blade (shaft) diameter along the screw axis from the head top outward. head_types: how a screw head is told from the manifest (name and mesh) and which drive it has; tools: drive size -> bit across-flats (or tip size) and the blade diameter of a precision driver that carries it. 'standard' values come from the named standard, 'assumption' values are typical precision-screwdriver blades, not measured on the owner's set: replace them with the owner's driver and every number follows.

path._doc: The path runs from start_offset_mm above the head top to the larger of min_length_mm (straight access behind the head for a driver blade plus fingers, as the mount check's DRIVER_L) and the distance at which the axis leaves the body's bounding box, capped at max_length_mm. max_length_mm 100 = the blade of a long precision driver (assumption: catalogue precision drivers carry 40-100 mm blades; the handle behind it can tilt and is not modelled); was 250 (the body box), which counted parts no driver blade reaches. Parts on another limb than the screw's (the other leg, an arm) are left out of the path: that limb is posed away or not yet attached while the screw is driven.

countersunk.source: ISO 10642 hex socket countersunk (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

pan_phillips.match: thread family PA* (self-tapping screws for plastic)
pan_phillips.source: ISO 7049 / DIN 7981 pan head cross recess (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

flange_button.source: assumption: hex socket as the button head (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

button.match: metric thread, head height under 0.7 x thread diameter and head diameter about 1.9 x thread diameter
button.source: ISO 7380-1 hex socket button head (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

socket_cap.match: metric thread, head height about the thread diameter
socket_cap.source: ISO 4762 hex socket head cap (head-type recognition; drive sizes: see tools)

hex_key.size_source: socket_cap M2 1.5 / M2.5 2.0 mm: ASME B18.3.1M metric socket head cap screw table (same sizes as ISO 4762), https://torqbolt.com/asme-b18-3-1m-socket-head-cap-screws-dimensions-standards-specifications; socket_cap M3 2.5 / M4 3.0 and every button, flange_button and countersunk size: assumption (common values, not checked against the standard texts). ISO 7380-1 button heads start at M3 (https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7380-1): the M2 / M2.5 button sizes are non-standard parts, assumption
hex_key.blade_source: assumption: precision hex driver blade, typical 3 mm to 2 mm AF and 4 mm above

phillips.size_source: assumption by analogy: ISO 7045 cross-recess numbers are 0 for M2 and 1 for M2.5 / M3 (type Z table, https://cdefasteners.com/sites/default/files/product-specs/meti7045pozi.pdf); the PA self-tapping screws are not ISO 7045 parts, so their recess sizes are an assumption until the screws' own data sheet or a measurement replaces them
